originality.rationale: Inspected the full directly relevant 2025 affine multi-modal S5 preprint (two accessibility relations in its NP-hardness construction), the central discussion and open problems of 2026 Modal Fragments, the generalized modal satisfiability literature, and the classic full-Boolean S5 depth-reduction abstract. None of the compared implications establishes the one-agent affine-hull iff criterion, sharp dimension-plus-one compression and closed pointed-type census. Multiple actual semantic record searches were also compared by implication. Residual unindexed literature risk remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed, differently phrased or unavailable affine-modal expressibility paper could already contain the same theorem or its stronger equivalent.
The 2016 classical S5 normalization source was available as abstract only, so its full text was not used to assert an exhaustive negative coverage conclusion.
The claim does not extend to multi-agent S5 or Boolean connectives outside the affine clone; coverage comparisons have been made only for the defined scope.

value.rationale: A natural 2025–26 affine modal fragment has a complete and exact pointed semantic equivalence classification, even with arbitrary nested modalities, a sharp linear optimal finite-model-size theorem and a closed all-n enumeration. It establishes a basis-sensitive semantic invariant rather than a renamed S5 exercise or ad hoc census, and quantifies information lost without conjunction.
